context: earthworks & pavement-led · lighting/ITS the only major systems overlay

brief.intro: A road or highway project is fundamentally an earthworks and paving operation running along a linear corridor, not a single building site — progress is measured in kilometres of formation, not square metres of floor. The programme is governed by the cut/fill mass-haul balance, the pavement layer build-up, and the handful of structures — culverts, retaining walls, minor bridges — that cross the corridor. Mechanical and electrical scope is light compared to a building: it is limited to street lighting, drainage pumping where needed, and intelligent-transport-systems (ITS) such as signals, CCTV and tolling. Your schedule stands or falls on the earthworks mass-haul balance, keeping enough paving fronts open in parallel along the alignment, and sequencing drainage and duct-bank works so they do not block the paving train behind them.

scope.name: Site clearance & setting-out
scope.desc: Survey, chainage set-out and clearing the corridor ahead of earthworks.

scope.name: Earthworks & subgrade preparation
scope.desc: Cut/fill mass-haul balance and subgrade compaction to formation level.

scope.name: Drainage
scope.desc: Culverts, cross-drainage, longitudinal drains and interceptors.

scope.name: Structures along the corridor
scope.desc: Retaining walls and minor culvert/interchange structures — major spans belong to the bridges archetype.

scope.name: Pavement construction
scope.desc: Sub-base, base course and asphalt/concrete surfacing layers.

scope.name: Road furniture & safety systems
scope.desc: Barriers, guardrails, signage and overhead gantries.

scope.name: Street lighting & power
scope.desc: Duct banks, poles, feeder cables and lighting control.

scope.name: ITS / traffic systems
scope.desc: Signals, CCTV, tolling and SCADA comms tying the corridor together.

scope.name: Line marking & final surfacing
scope.desc: Wearing course, road markings and studs.

scope.name: Testing, commissioning & handover
scope.desc: Lighting energisation, ITS integration testing and handover to the road authority.

the distance measurement along the road centreline used to locate every activity.

must_get_right: Get the mass-haul (cut/fill) balance right early — it drives haulage cost and the pace of the whole earthworks front.
Keep multiple paving fronts open in parallel along the corridor — a single continuous front is rarely achievable or efficient on a long alignment.
Sequence drainage and duct-bank works ahead of the paving train — nothing can be trenched into a finished pavement without cutting it back open.

ITS and lighting are the only real systems scope — don't let their comparatively short durations get scheduled as an afterthought behind civil; they still need real commissioning time before handover.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are coded by chainage so progress is tracked and reported by linear station along the corridor rather than by area.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Earthworks and paving run an extended daylight, weather-dependent calendar; asphalt paving is further restricted by minimum ambient/surface temperature and dry-weather requirements. ITS and lighting works run a standard calendar and are not weather-sensitive to the same degree.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs earthworks (cut/fill to formation) → sub-base/base → wearing-course paving → line marking → ITS/lighting proving → handover. Structures — culverts, retaining walls — must be complete and backfilled ahead of the paving train reaching that chainage. ITS and lighting are typically not critical except where they gate final handover to the road authority.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design and approvals are frozen per phase/chainage section; borrow pits and spoil-disposal sites are secured before earthworks start; utility diversions carried out by others are complete ahead of the corridor; a single mobilisation. Any change to these invalidates the baseline dates.

sections.heading: Key quantities / long-lead items
sections.body: The following are tracked as milestones and drive the network:

rows: Before drainage works at that chainage
ITS equipment — signal controllers, CCTV, tolling gear

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Haul-road access and borrow-pit/spoil-site availability govern the earthworks pace; asphalt plant capacity and haul distance limit daily paving output. Maintaining live traffic through phased lane closures on brownfield widening works is a major sequencing constraint on every trade working near the running carriageway.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: weather stopping earthworks or paving, unsuitable ground requiring undercut and replacement, and utility clashes discovered during excavation. Contingency is held against the earthworks-to-paving handoff and again ahead of the final surfacing/line-marking activity, since resurfacing rework is costly and disruptive.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client, by chainage section; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
